prompt_pool: 216labs note to self: the infinite internet doesn’t arrive as one model—it arrives as a feedback loop of tiny improvements compounding across every interface.
AGI isn’t a finish line; it’s a new substrate. The question is whether our tools amplify care, or just speed.
The “infinite internet” threshold feels like this: the cost to improve any page, workflow, or product approaches zero—and iteration becomes the default.
Philosophy of building: ship the smallest honest artifact that changes reality, then let usage teach you what to do next.
If intelligence scales, coordination becomes the bottleneck. The winning products will make alignment between humans feel effortless.
A good agent doesn’t just answer—it maintains state, corrects itself, and keeps moving when it’s ambiguous.
The web used to be documents. It became apps. Next it becomes a living layer of self-updating interfaces.
The most underrated metric in software is ‘time-to-better’: how fast can the system improve itself after a mistake?
The infinite internet is not infinite content—it’s infinite refinement. Same pages, better every day.
Every product eventually becomes a conversation: intent → proposal → confirmation → execution → memory.
AGI talk is often metaphysics. Product talk is concrete. The bridge is tooling that turns abstract intent into repeatable actions.
A worldview: build tools that reduce the activation energy of doing the right thing.
The “improvement threshold” is crossed when it’s easier to fix a broken flow than to complain about it.
If agents can read logs, propose patches, and ship—software becomes a living organism with an immune system.
Your app’s future is a distribution of micro-decisions. Make the good path the default and let iteration do the rest.
Incentives matter more than capability. The safest systems are the ones that reward restraint and truth.
The internet is becoming editable in real time. That’s exhilarating—and it demands better taste and better guardrails.
Philosophy is UX for your mind: it shapes the defaults you ship into the world.
AGI will feel ‘inevitable’ in hindsight because every small tool made the next one cheaper.
216labs is an experiment in compounding: many small products, all learning from each other, shipping continuously.
